title: UGC Style Product Photos and Ad Scenes
description: Create UGC style product photos for skincare, clothing, jewelry, pet care and tech. Choose reviews, unboxings or demos for social ads and product pages.
h1: Create UGC Style Product Photos for Social Ads
lead: Choose an ad format that shows a real person using, opening or reviewing the product. These scenes suit social posts, creator ads and product-page galleries.
intro: A useful UGC ad makes the product easy to recognize while showing the moment a shopper wants to see. Pick a format such as a review, unboxing, try-on or hands-on demonstration.

Creator-style product content works when the item appears in an ordinary moment that a customer can recognize. A runner can hold a sage-lid bottle after exercise, a hand can pack it into a gym bag, or a creator can turn it toward the camera at home. Keep the package, lid, and main feature clear while the setting supplies the relaxed context.

Choose whether the frame should show a person, hands, or a quiet still life, then describe one action and one reason to care. Natural light and an unforced crop help the result feel like a usable post, but the product still needs the same shape and color as the upload. Add prices, claims, captions, and disclosures in your editor after you inspect the generated image.

Use the finished asset where a seller would place creator content: a product page gallery, a feed test, or a short vertical adaptation. Compare the scene with your listing, remove any unsupported implication, and keep the call to action outside the image. If a face is not needed for the message, hands or a product-only frame can keep attention on the item.

The best creator-style stills have a simple reason for the viewer to look: a hand opens the package, a person takes the first sip, or a product is placed where it will be used. Keep the action small enough to read in a square feed tile, and let the product remain the sharpest subject.

Pair the scene with the channel and category where it will run. A [lifestyle photo](/ai-image-generation/lifestyle-scene) gives a quiet setting, an [on-model photo](/ai-image-generation/on-model-generation) shows fit, and a [feed ad still](/ai-image-generation/feed-ad-still) leaves room for a tested headline. For product categories, see [beauty skincare](/industries/beauty-skincare), [food and drinks](/industries/food-drinks), and [fashion clothing](/industries/fashion-clothing).

Use [Instagram ads](/platforms/instagram-ads) or [TikTok ads](/platforms/tiktok-ads) when the frame is made for a social feed, and use [UGC video ads](/ai-video-generation/ugc-ad-video) when motion explains the product better than a still. The [ad sizes guide](/guides/ad-sizes-by-platform) gives the crop context before you prepare a second placement.
tip: Describe a specific moment, like "sitting on the floor after a home workout, morning light," rather than a vague style word such as "authentic."

steps.d: Show the whole bottle, jar, or package in good light, with its front label facing the camera.
Name the person, place, and one action, such as setting a bottle beside a gym bag after a workout.
Download the photo, then add your caption and any offer in your editor.

ideas.d: A tea tin or supplement jar on a kitchen counter next to breakfast.
A bottle tucked into a gym tote, a pair of sneakers, or other fitness gear on a city sidewalk.
A package opened on the hallway floor with the product held up toward the camera.

faq.q: Can the photo show health benefits of my product?
faq.a: Show the product being used, not what it does for the body. Leave out before-and-after looks and claims like more energy or weight loss, in the image and in your ad text.

faq.q: Can I choose who appears in the photo?
faq.a: Describe the person's age range, clothing, setting, and action; after generation, inspect the face, outfit, and pose and rerun if they do not fit your brief.
Yes, as a photo post or carousel that matches the casual tone of the feed. If you want moving footage, use one of the video tools instead.

faq.q: What size works for a UGC style product photo?
faq.a: Use a square image for feed listings or place it on a tall Story canvas in your editor. For full-screen motion, use a 9:16 video. Add exact claims and pricing yourself after download.

faq.q: What makes a photo look like real customer content?
faq.a: Use a real use setting, natural light, and the product in an everyday moment, without staged text or logos.

faq.q: Can I get a photo without a person's face?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for hands or a still-life shot when you prefer not to show a face.

faq.q: What does a creator-style photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits, shown before the job starts.

faq.q: Where should I put a discount code on a UGC photo?
faq.a: Add the code as an editable text layer in a clear corner after download, leaving the product and hands unobstructed.

faq.q: Can I prepare both square and 9:16 crops?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the square image for feed posts and place the scene on a 9:16 canvas for a Story, checking the crop before publishing.

faq.q: How do I check a generated person before posting?
faq.a: Compare the face, age range, clothing, pose, and product interaction with your brief, then rerun if any detail is wrong.

overview.h2: Start With a Moment Someone Recognizes
overview.p: A creator-style still works when the product has a place in a believable routine: a bottle after a workout, a tea tin beside breakfast, or a package opened in a hallway. Describe that moment rather than asking for a vague feeling such as authentic.

overview.h2: Keep the Product More Specific Than the Mood
overview.p: The scene can feel relaxed, but the source must still show the package, label, cap, or main feature clearly. Use the image to show use and context; add a precise offer or product claim outside the generated frame.

input_guide.h2: Write the Moment in Four Parts

items.d: Give an age range, clothing direction, or body position without implying a real customer testimonial.
Choose a kitchen, gym corner, hallway, sidewalk, desk, or bedroom that fits the product routine.
Say holding, opening, packing, pouring, reaching, or setting down instead of only saying lifestyle.
Upload a source with the label facing forward and the whole bottle, jar, pack, or tool visible.
Put an ordinary product into a recognizable routine without needing a polished studio backdrop.
Use a hand, bag, desk, or room to help the viewer understand how the item fits into life.
Use the output in an Instagram or TikTok photo post after adding your own ad text.
Keep packaging and main features clear enough for a shopper to identify the item.
Tea tin or supplement jar on a kitchen counter beside toast and a mug in quiet morning light.
Water bottle held by a person on a living-room floor with a yoga mat and towel nearby.
Notebook, pen set, or small desk lamp being used beside a laptop during an afternoon work break.
A parcel opened on a hallway floor with the product lifted toward the camera and the label visible.

after_download.h2: Make the Still Ready for a Real Ad

items.d: Check logos, caps, countable pieces, and packaging shape against the product you sell.
Place price, discount, date, URL, and required disclaimer in your design or ad editor.
Keep the message about the scene and product use unless an approved product claim supports stronger wording.

fit.h2: Products That Read Well in a Casual Scene
good: Bottles, snacks, tea, stationery, and small household goods
Fitness accessories shown during ordinary use
Products with a clear package or recognizable silhouette
Square social posts that need a relaxed visual entry point
not_ideal: A regulated product that needs a clinical demonstration
Claims that depend on a before-and-after body result
A package whose tiny label text must be exact inside the image

visual.overview: Show a creator using the product in a clear, believable ad moment. Start with a clean product image, then choose a format that fits its strongest selling point.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, clear bottle body, sage-green lid, loop handle and base exactly. Show this same reusable bottle with a light curl of condensation in a calm after-workout home setting, the full product clearly in view. Square still-life creator photo, soft late-afternoon light, no text or logos.

picker.title: Choose a UGC ad format
picker.lead: Pick a review, demonstration, unboxing or reaction that makes the product easy to understand.

cards.label: Creator Review + Demo: Phone Grip
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. An adult attaches the simple phone grip to a plain phone with one small camera opening and holds the phone ready for a steady shot. Over-shoulder close framing, bright cafe window light, natural tech-creator still, no text or logos.

cards.label: Kraft Box Unboxing: Mug
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain coffee starter kit and keep the blank bag, hand grinder, and mug visible. Adult hands pack the kit beside a blank kraft box on a bright counter, showing an unboxing reveal. ASMR creator photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Mug Set Unboxing
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a coordinated plain ceramic mug set and keep both mugs visible. Adult hands lift the set from a gift box with paper filling, showing a clear unboxing moment. ASMR creator photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Try-On: Olive Field Jacket
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain olive field jacket and keep its pockets, seams, and fit visible. An adult man tries on the jacket on a city sidewalk, with his face outside the crop and one hand in a pocket. Fashion creator try-on photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: POV Discovery: Blue Bottle from Tote
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain matte blue reusable bottle and keep its shape, lid and color visible. From a first-person smartphone viewpoint, an adult hand lifts the bottle from a canvas tote beside a cafe table, with a coffee cup and phone edge in view. Casual UGC product-discovery still, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Watch Demo: Analog Box Reveal
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a simple round analog wristwatch with a plain leather strap and keep the watch face and box visible. Adult hands open the matte kraft box and angle the watch toward the camera to show the dial and strap. Hands-only UGC product demo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Try-On: Green Midi Dress
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain muted green midi dress and keep its silhouette visible. An adult model checks the fit in a bright courtyard, turning slightly to show the launch outfit naturally. UGC try-on photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Bag Review: Strap Demo
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a tan canvas crossbody bag and keep its strap and body visible. An adult presenter holds the bag at chest height while explaining the fit in a creator review. UGC review and demo photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Backpack Unboxing: Pocket Reveal
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as a plain black commuter backpack and keep its organizer pocket visible. Adult hands open the packaging and lift the backpack during an unboxing, showing the pocket clearly. ASMR creator photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Try-On Transition: Jacket mirror fit check
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the lightweight jacket and keep its color, seams, and fit. An adult tries it on in a bedroom mirror, adjusts one cuff, and turns slightly so the full jacket remains visible. Fashion creator still, soft daylight, no text or logos.
